terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: SkyPack is a free service for searching and comparing travel. By using the site, you agree to these terms.

sections.h: We don't sell tickets or stays
p: We are not a carrier, travel agent or hotel and don't accept payments. The “Go to seller” button opens a partner's site; booking, payment, changes and refunds follow that site's rules.
Some links are affiliate links: if you buy a ticket after following one, we may earn a commission. Your price doesn't change because of it.
Prices come from third-party sources. Some are cached (found earlier) — we always show when a price was found. The seller shows the final price, baggage and fare terms before payment.
If layover or baggage details are unknown, we say so — it doesn't mean there are none.

“Our pick” and the scores are calculated by code using an open formula (see “How we calculate”). The AI assistant only parses the request and explains the finished result; it can make mistakes — double-check what matters before buying.

Notifications are a free convenience with no guarantees: the price may change between the check and your visit, and a check may be delayed. You can unsubscribe at any time from the email, the bot or your account.
Don't use the service for automated data collection or load: the number of requests is limited. We may change or discontinue features without notice.
The service is provided “as is”. We are not responsible for the actions of carriers, hotels and sellers, for changes in prices or schedules, or for decisions made solely on the basis of our scores.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: We collect the minimum data needed for features to work and don't sell it. Search works without an account.

p: Account (if you create one): username, name, optional email, password hash (scrypt — we don't know the password itself), Google or Telegram ID if you sign in with them. Search history and saved searches (up to the last 200), favorites — flights, stays and ready-made trips (up to 200: offer parameters, dates, price and when it was obtained), saved trips (up to 50: route, dates, chosen flight and stay, prices at the time of saving). Chats with the AI assistant — only if you turned on chat sync (up to 30 chats); turning it off deletes them from the account. Optional profile: interface language, currency, country of residence, home and favourite airports, search preferences, your own photo (up to 300 KB, visible only to you); if you sign in with Google — the address of your Google photo (shown through our server, your browser does not contact Google). Sign-in sessions: sign-in date, last activity and a coarse device description (browser and OS, e.g. “Chrome · macOS”) — no IP; notification settings (channels, frequency, quiet hours and your time zone).

Price alerts: the route (or stay city), dates or period and trip length, number of adults, required baggage, the condition (threshold or drop) and the contact for notifications — email or a Telegram chat; a log of checks and sent notifications (prices, no email texts). The log of routine checks is kept for 30 days; you can delete a subscription with its history at any time.
Price history and visits to partner sites are stored without being tied to a person: route, price, source, partner domain — without IP or account.

Anonymous usage statistics: which actions happen (a search started, found results or not, details opened, a trip saved, a click to a seller) with short labels like “flights” or “stays” — without an account, session, cookies, IP, routes, dates or query texts. Kept for 90 days. If your browser asks not to be tracked (Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track), we record nothing.

A public link to a saved trip exists only if you turn it on and stops working as soon as you turn it off. It shows the route, dates, flight, stay and prices at the time of saving — without your name, trip title, budget or own expenses.

Only necessary ones: the sign-in session cookie (httpOnly, up to 30 days), a temporary cookie during Google sign-in, and the interface language cookie (NEXT_LOCALE, one year — only the chosen language). There are no advertising or analytics cookies. After sign-in we set the language cookie from your profile.

Your browser (localStorage / sessionStorage) keeps: the theme, AI chat history, the list of your notifications, the last search tab, and without an account — favorites and saved trips too (after sign-in they move to your account); in the tab — the trips selected for comparison and the “Undo last choice” steps. Chat history doesn't reach the server unless you turned on “Sync chats across devices” yourself (account only); you can delete it in the chat.
Recent searches (up to 6: route, dates, people and filters — as in the page address) are also kept only in this browser; you can remove them with “Clear”.
Search parameters (cities, dates, number of people) — price providers: SerpApi (Google Flights) and Travelpayouts.

The text of your requests to the AI assistant and the search results — DeepSeek, for parsing and explanation. We don't log this text; chats are stored in your account only if you turned on chat sync. Don't put personal data in the chat. If you're signed in, the assistant searches with your profile settings: your home airport and currency are part of the conversation context, while preferred airlines and amenities are applied only by our scoring code and are not sent to the model.
Infrastructure: Vercel (site), Render (server), Supabase (database, EU — Frankfurt), Sentry (error reports without personal data). Notifications — via Telegram or email.

Stays map: your browser loads map tiles directly from OpenFreeMap (tiles.openfreemap.org, OpenStreetMap data) — that service sees your IP address and the part of the map you're viewing. The map loads only in “Map” mode.
Account data — until you delete the account. A session lasts up to 30 days, email links — from 1 to 24 hours. Search history in the account — up to the last 200 entries.

In your account you can change your data, clear the search history, unlink Google or Telegram and delete the account completely — together with notifications, history, favorites, saved trips and assistant chats and profile photo. You can also request a copy of your data or its correction.

howItWorks.title: How we calculate prices and scores
howItWorks.intro: All numbers on the site are calculated by code using fixed rules. The AI doesn't make up prices or choose the “best” option — it only explains the result.

p: Flight search asks several sources at once: live Google Flights prices via SerpApi and seller prices from the Aviasales search cache (Travelpayouts), marked with when the price was found. Flexible dates start from free cached prices, and the live source checks only the cheapest dates. The same flight from several sellers is one card showing the cheapest seller; the rest are under “Seller offers” with each one's terms (baggage, price freshness), and for the first flight in the list we check sellers right away, for the others “Compare sellers and check the price” checks live which airlines and agencies sell the flight on Google Flights. The list is ordered by the lowest cost for all passengers and the whole trip in your currency, including the baggage you need when its price is known. This is the lowest price among the sources checked in this search, not a guaranteed lowest price on the whole market: we don't query Skyscanner, Kiwi.com, Trip.com, Expedia or airline websites directly — there is no open access to their prices, and their offers reach us only through these sources.

The flight price is shown for the whole party of the search (for one adult — for that adult): children and infants are at their own fare, we don't guess it. The stay price is for the whole room with taxes.

Every price shows how fresh it is: “just checked” (live source, up to 30 min), “cached” (found earlier, up to 3 days), “approximate” (unknown when found) or “worth re-checking” (older). Identical searches made at the same time go to the source only once.

You choose the currency (EUR, USD, GBP, PLN) for flights, stays and trips. Prices are shown as the source gives them; if it gave another currency, we convert it for comparison at the ECB reference rate and mark it “≈ … approximate”. The seller may charge in its own currency at your bank's rate — this is not a guaranteed charge. We don't hide cents: a fractional price is shown with cents.

First we remove options that break your mandatory requirements (filters, “direct only”, baggage the fare doesn't allow): they are never recommended, however cheap, and above the list we say how many were hidden and why. The rest are ranked: score = price + known fee for the selected baggage + cost of extra travel time + stop penalty + risks (short or overnight layover, separate tickets, airport change, night departure or arrival) + mismatch with your settings (preferred airlines and departure time). The lower, the better value. The weight of time depends on “What matters more”: price, balance or time.

An unknown baggage fee and unknown layover details only add a warning, not a penalty. “Why this option?” shows concrete reasons from the same data: for example, how much more an option costs than the cheapest and how many hours of travel it saves.

First we remove stays that fail your filters. The rest are scored: score = price per night + distance to the centre and transit + rating adjustment + cancellation terms + preferred amenities from your settings that are missing. Ratings with few reviews are pulled towards the average, so a single perfect score doesn't beat hundreds of reviews. “Why this option?” compares it with the cheapest and the top-rated in money for the whole stay, kilometres and rating points.

Trip total = tickets for everyone + baggage fees + the stay for all nights with taxes + costs you added yourself. Confirmed (source prices for these dates), indicative (cached prices, your costs) and unknown items are shown separately; unknown items aren't included in the total, and transfers without reliable data aren't added. The stay runs from the arrival date to the return departure date in local time: a night flight won't get you a hotel on the wrong dates. Scenarios: “Economy” — the lowest total with your conditions; “Optimal” — the price plus the “cost” of travel time, stops, the stay's location and rating, and inconvenient arrival or departure times; “Comfort” — the fewest stops and least travel time, then the stay's rating and proximity. The choice is within the budget, and if none fits — marked as over budget. Identical scenarios aren't duplicated. “Find a cheaper option” checks other dates (±3 days, the same number of nights), nearby airports, other flights and stays of the same type without changing your conditions, and shows how many options were checked: this is part of the market, not a guarantee of the lowest price.

For each combination we show how many nights are full (a late arrival from 23:00 or an early return before 07:00 “eats” a night you paid for), the total travel time and how much of it is waiting at layovers. “Why this option?” compares it with “Budget” and “Comfort”: how much more or less it costs, how many hours of travel, full nights and stops it saves, how much better the stay is and whether it fits the budget.
It parses a plain-language request into search parameters (airport codes and dates are checked by code) and explains the result. Every number in the explanation is checked against the search results.
